caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 72 of 2011
lawyer:
Muhammad Jamiruddin Sircar, Senior Advocate instructed by Wahidullah, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioners
Biswajit Deb Nath, Deputy Attorney General instructed by Zahirul Islam, Advocate-on-Record ------ The Respondents
parties:
Akbor Ali and Ors. ----- Petitioners
Vs.
The State ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali, J: This criminal petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 16.08.2010 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Appeal No. 24001 of 2010 summarily rejecting the application filed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure arising out of the judgment and order dated 02.10.2007 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Appeal No. 942 of 2005 affirming the judgment and order dated 15.01.2005 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Dinajpur in Session Case No. 13 of 1996, arising out of Chirir Bandar Police Station Case. No. 2(10)/95 corresponding to G.R. No. 1188 of 1995 convicting the petitioners under section 302/34 of the Penal Code and sentencing them to suffer imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Tk. 5,000/- each, in default to suffer imprisonment for 5(five) months more. 

 2. Facts of the case, which led to the filing of the instant criminal petition for leave to appeal, are that after the petitioners were convicted and sentenced under section 302/34 of the Penal Code, they preferred appeal before the High Court Division, being Criminal Appeal No. 942 of 2005. After hearing the parties concerned, including the learned Advocate representing the appellants, by an exhaustive judgment and order dated 02.10.2007 a Division Bench of the High Court Division dismissed the appeal thereby confirming the Conviction and sentence awarded by the trial Court. After a lapse of two and half years the convicted accused filed a miscellaneous petition before the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure agitating grounds similar to those placed before the High Court Division at the time of the appeal. Particular emphasis was on the ground that the conviction of the convict appellants should have been considered under the first and second part of section 304 of the Penal Code. 

 3. After hearing the parties concerned the Division Bench of the High Court Division, which heard the criminal miscellaneous case, rejected the petition summarily on the ground that such an application is peculiar and unheard of where the petitioners were asking the High Court Division to entertain an appeal against a judgment of the High Court Division in the guise of an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. It was observed by the High Court Division that the question of making review or interfering with the judgment passed by another Division Bench assuming the jurisdiction of the Appellate Division does not arise at all. 

 7. There is no provision within the Code of Criminal Procedure for any second appeal, review or revision of any decision arrived at after hearing an appeal against conviction and sentence. We, therefore, find that the instant criminal petition for leave to appeal is misconceived and without any merit.
